question: A 45-year-old man presents with a chief complaint of pain in the great toe. He has a history of gout, which is under control. He was diagnosed with diabetes 5 years ago and is currently taking metformin. He was recently diagnosed with hypertension and was placed on a hypertensive drug. He is a non-smoker and does not abuse alcohol. The family history is significant for ischemic heart disease in his father. His current blood pressure is 136/84 mm Hg and the pulse is 78/min. The physical examination did not reveal any abnormalities. He uses over-the-counter multivitamin supplements. Which of the following drugs could have resulted in these symptoms?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: Metformin -> can cause lactic acidosis -> presenting as pain in the great toe -> 80% CHAIN: Hypertensive drug (possible ACE inhibitor) -> can cause hyperkalemia -> exacerbating gout symptoms -> 70% CHAIN: Thiazide diuretics -> can increase uric acid levels -> worsening gout symptoms -> 75% CHAIN: Calcium channel blockers (CCBs) -> may not directly worsen gout symptoms -> 60% CHAIN: Beta-blockers -> can increase uric acid levels -> potentially worsening gout symptoms -> 70% CHAIN: Angiotensin II receptor blockers (ARBs) -> generally do not worsen gout symptoms -> 80%
analysis: Given the patient's history of gout and current medications, the drug that could potentially result in worsening symptoms is thiazide diuretics.
